_comment: I2-upstream. A realistic, hand-shaped capture of the EventBridge "CloudWatch Alarm State Change" event that the culprit-alarm-state-change rule routes to the culprit-dispatch Lambda when culprit-App-High transitions to ALARM. Lets the Lambda be unit-tested offline with zero AWS calls. IMPORTANT: detail.state.reasonData (and detail.previousState.reasonData) is deliberately a STRING, not a nested object -- CloudWatch always JSON-encodes it as a string, which is exactly why the Lambda needs a real json.loads() and why a plain EventBridge input transformer cannot read it (docs/architecture.md §2, "A Lambda, not an EventBridge API Destination"). This file's datapoints, threshold and timestamps are illustrative only and are NOT kept in sync with the live example in docs/contracts/dispatch-payload.json -- that file is refreshed from real culprit-dispatch CloudWatch Logs output and will drift from whatever numbers are hand-shaped here. Treat this file as a shape/schema fixture (what the Lambda parses: reasonData as a JSON string, recentDatapoints, threshold, timestamp) rather than a value-for-value match to the dispatch payload example. Namespace/alarm/unit below match the real EC2 app (HackathonDemo, RequestLatency in seconds, dimension App=bad-app-ec2) -- a synthetic feed in namespace=Culprit used to also produce this shape via culprit-Latency-High; it was deleted (docs/decisions.md §9).
